parsed.title: Discussion about working abroad in Slovakia, Austria and language requirements

topics.title: People living or who have lived abroad

claims.text: Some participants live in or have lived in Slovakia, Austria, Poland, and Austria since 2025.
One participant has been in Austria since November 2025.

topics.title: Finding jobs abroad and application experience

claims.text: Finding a job abroad was hard but the speaker succeeded within two months.
LinkedIn was recommended as a job search platform.
The speaker sent about 100 applications and got only three interviews.
Most job postings require local language proficiency (about 95%).
There are cases where candidates with little language knowledge are still hired.
Higher education rarely matters for hiring decisions.
Salary for the speaker’s position was low, comparable to minimum wage.
Employers often ask for B2 language level, sometimes B1, but certificates are rarely required.

topics.title: Language expectations in the job market

claims.text: German is the primary language spoken in Austria, but English is also used.
Many companies list local language as a requirement, but some accept English.
The speaker is learning the local language because of daily discomfort.
One participant feels less confident speaking English outside of work.
Attending international events makes English usage easier.
A partner living in Austria for over 10 years is skeptical about the country’s future.
